title: On-prem air-gapped ops requirements - Capstone Bank discovery
next_steps: Redwood to send Air Gap security pack + signed offline installer link
Schedule on-site feasibility call for week of 2025-04-28
SE to run compatibility checklist against Capstone hardware and send back notes
Provide draft pilot scope and pricing for a 3-month private pilot
action_items: Liam Chen: validate driver and CUDA compatibility with Capstone GPU inventory by 2025-04-18
Aisha Patel: share SOC2/ISO pack and previous on-prem compliance case studies by 2025-04-13
Sophie Lin: provide hardware inventory and change control window details by 2025-04-15
summary: Discovery focused on on-prem air-gapped deployment feasibility. Customer requires FIPS/HSM key management, strictly no egress, signed offline installer, and long maintenance windows. Hardware constraints include mixed GPU fleet (V100/T4), no internet for nodes, and long patch cycles. Discussed pilot scope, benchmarks, and next steps for feasibility and security documentation.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-04-11 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Aisha (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Jorge (Head of AI, Capstone), Sophie (Infra Architect, Capstone), Markus (Security Officer, Capstone)

00:00:05 Aisha (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for making time. Quick intro, I m Aisha, I'm the AE on the account, and with me is Liam from the SE team. Want to hear about Capstone's constraints and see how Redwood Private could map.
00:00:18 Jorge (Capstone): Hi, thanks. We re on a pretty tight compliance regime — financial services, EU+US data residency, and a full air-gap requirement for model inference in production. So no outbound internet from inference nodes.
00:00:34 Sophie (Capstone): And to add, our ops team only allows signed, vetted binaries and we have a change control window of two weekends per quarter for updates. Patch windows are long.
00:00:47 Liam (Redwood SE): Understood. That aligns with some other bank deployments we've worked on. Quick clarifying question: when you say air-gap, do you mean absolutely no egress from the inference hosts, or can control plane traffic go out through a jump box?
00:01:02 Markus (Capstone): Absolutely no egress from the hosts. Everything has to go through our bastion or staging zone. If we can have a control plane inside the VPC that is customer-owned and only talks to the management plane via an offline sync, that's preferable.
00:01:20 Aisha (Redwood AE): Right, so that would point to our Redwood Private option — customer-managed control plane or even fully on-prem. Liam, do we have a standard offline installer and signed artifact flow?
00:01:31 Liam (Redwood SE): We do. We call it the air-gap bundle internally. It's a signed tarball with hashes, plus an install tool. For air-gapped customers we provide a checksum file and a signing certificate chain. In previous deployments we've worked with a KMS/HSM for key wrapping.
00:01:52 Jorge (Capstone): HSM is a hard requirement. We use Thales Luna and require FIPS-140 validated crypto for key material. Also, audit logs must be shipped to our SIEM — but since there's no egress, we expect the logs to be collected internally and then batch-uploaded during maintenance windows.
00:02:10 Sophie (Capstone): Another constraint: our GPU fleet is mixed. We have older V100 nodes, some T4s on edge servers, and a small pool of a100 equivalent on dedicated racks. Updating drivers requires change control sign-off; we can t have automatic driver upgrades.
00:02:28 Liam (Redwood SE): Got it. For driver management we support pinned driver versions in the runtime. The runtime can run on multiple CUDA versions but we typically test on the specific builds. We'll need your exact kernel/driver list.
00:02:40 Sophie (Capstone): We'll provide the inventory. Also, network policy — no DNS lookups to external services from inference hosts; all model artifacts must be locally available. How does Redwood handle model updates in that scenario?
00:02:53 Liam (Redwood SE): Two options: a) Signed offline model bundle you push to your artifact repo; b) a customer-hosted internal registry that our control plane (deployed in your network) can pull from during a maintenance window. For strict air-gap we usually do signed bundles and a documented offline upgrade process.
00:03:10 Markus (Capstone): We need to see the cryptographic verification steps. If it's a tarball, we want the full chain — signing key usage, rotation policy, and how the system handles an interrupted update.
00:03:23 Aisha (Redwood AE): We'll share our offline installer docs and a checklist. Liam, can you walk through the high-level component diagram for Capstone?
00:03:31 Liam (Redwood SE): Sure. Picture three layers: control plane (customer managed in VPC), inference pool (air-gapped GPU nodes), and a management jump host for operator interactions. The control plane can be deployed as Docker/k8s manifests. For on-prem we also support an OVA style deploy. Communication between control plane and inference pool is over internal signed mTLS and we support mutual cert rotation via HSM.
00:03:56 Sophie (Capstone): You said OVA — our virtualization team prefers images we can import into our hypervisor. Is OVA supported for your private package?
00:04:05 Liam (Redwood SE): Yes, we provide VM images for a few hypervisors, and a containerized path. OVA is commonly used. We can also provide a systemd-based unit for bare metal.
00:04:14 Jorge (Capstone): Performance is key. We need predictable 95th percentile latency under 200ms for short text generations in peak loads. How do you guarantee latency without egress to your hosted fallback?
00:04:28 Liam (Redwood SE): Good question. In private deployments we rely on the local serving runtime — model selection, quantization, and batching are all local. We provide a set of verified model variants to keep memory and latency predictable. We also ship KV cache and prefix cache tooling to reduce per-token compute. Note that some model optimizations require specific CUDA capabilities; we'll confirm which variants map to V100 vs A100.
00:04:50 Markus (Capstone): If we have to degrade to lower-cost model variants during peak, is that something Redwood supports automatically or do we need to manage rollouts?
00:05:00 Aisha (Redwood AE): Redwood supports canary and automatic fallback policies, but for air-gapped setups we usually configure rollouts via your operations procedures. We can provide the policy DSL and a recommended automation runbook, but execution typically stays inside your change windows.
00:05:17 Sophie (Capstone): Another operational note — we need offline metrics export. Prometheus scrapes are fine, but we need a way to snapshot traces and download them for offline analysis.
00:05:28 Liam (Redwood SE): We expose Prometheus metrics and a trace archive tool. You can bundle traces and ship them to your SIEM during windows. We also have a lightweight observability bundle that runs locally.
00:05:40 Speaker 1: (inaudible)
00:05:45 Jorge (Capstone): On the compliance front, can you map where data is stored temporarily? We have strict rules about tokens and ephemeral cache — all must be purged on schedule or encrypted at rest.
00:05:57 Liam (Redwood SE): The runtime stores KV cache on local encrypted volumes. All temp files are cleared on process restart unless configured otherwise. We can point to the config flag and default retention policy. Encryption at rest can be integrated with your HSM/KMS for key wrapping.
00:06:12 Sophie (Capstone): And audit logs — we need immutability guarantees. Are logs append-only and can they be exported with signed digests?
00:06:21 Liam (Redwood SE): We can sign log bundles at the source before they leave the inference zone. Logs are append-only and we include sequence numbers and hashes for tamper-evidence. The signed bundle can be validated against the signing key that you control in the HSM.
00:06:35 Markus (Capstone): Sounds promising. How about process for emergency fixes? If we discover a P0 security issue in the runtime, what's the turnaround? We may need to apply a hotfix out of cycle.
00:06:46 Aisha (Redwood AE): We have an enterprise incident playbook for on-prem customers. Typically, we provide a signed hotfix artifact and a guided runbook; we also offer an optional on-call premium support that includes out-of-window assistance and on-site engineers if agreed in the contract.
00:07:02 Jorge (Capstone): Cost question — how do you price private deployments vs dedicated hosted? We need unit economics across pilots and production scale.
00:07:12 Aisha (Redwood AE): Pricing for Private is typically a platform license plus per-GPU seat for the runtime, and optional premium support. We'll send a draft pricing sheet tailored to your initial pilot size. For comparison, Dedicated reserved capacity is usage-based with a monthly commit; we can include both in the draft.
00:07:28 Sophie (Capstone): For the pilot we want a 3-month technical pilot with a capped 10-node inference pool and an evaluation plan: latency targets, throughput targets, and quality thresholds. We also need to measure unit costs per 1k words.
00:07:42 Liam (Redwood SE): That pilot scope is reasonable. For the evaluation we'll run benchmark suites locally — we ask customers to provide a representative prompt set (you can anonymize). We then benchmark on your hardware and produce a performance/cost report.
00:07:56 Jorge (Capstone): On the secret side, we use a centralized HSM for key operations. Can your runtime do in-HSM crypto ops so keys never leave?
00:08:07 Liam (Redwood SE): Yes, we support in-HSM signing/unwrap operations. Keys remain in the HSM, and the runtime calls the HSM via PKCS#11 or cloud HSM APIs, depending on your setup. We ve integrated with Thales and AWS CloudHSM in past deployments.
00:08:23 Sophie (Capstone): Minor note — our compliance team calls egress any outbound connection, even to vendor support endpoints. Are there ways for Redwood to provide telemetry without outbound egress?
00:08:34 Liam (Redwood SE): We do local telemetry snapshots and a handoff process where you can upload the snapshots to a secure Redwood S3 under a presigned link, or we can accept an offline transfer (sftp, hand-carry) depending on your policy.
00:08:48 Markus (Capstone): Good. We also run penetration tests quarterly — will Redwood allow a black-box pentest against the deployed runtime?
00:08:58 Aisha (Redwood AE): Yes, but we usually coordinate that through our security team so the scope is agreed and Redwood provides a point of contact. We'll also share our hardening guide beforehand.
00:09:10 Speaker 2 (inaudible):
00:09:15 Jorge (Capstone): One last technical detail — do you support quantized int8 models for V100? We d like to trade quality for latency/cost sometimes.
00:09:25 Liam (Redwood SE): We support several quantization paths. INT8 on V100 is possible but requires specific kernels and reduced batch sizes. We'll test quality regression on your prompt set as part of the pilot.
00:09:37 Sophie (Capstone): Ok great. Let's talk risk and blockers. Biggest blocker is our procurement — legal wants SLAs and indemnities for on-prem software, and security wants full artifact validation. We'll need a standard-enterprise contract for Private deployment.
00:09:52 Aisha (Redwood AE): We have an enterprise SLA template and previous contract language from other banks; I can circulate redlines. We'll also include the indemnity language for on-prem in the draft.
00:10:03 Jorge (Capstone): Timeline: our board wants a decision by end of Q2 if we can meet the compliance needs. Pilot ideally starts mid-May. Is that feasible?
00:10:14 Aisha (Redwood AE): If we get your hardware inventory and legal kickoff this week, a mid-May pilot start is feasible. Liam, is that operationally OK?
00:10:22 Liam (Redwood SE): Yes, assuming the compatibility check doesn't reveal blockers. We' ll need about two weeks to prepare the air-gap bundle and one week for on-site or remote install support.
00:10:33 Sophie (Capstone): We'll send inventory and change control calendar by 2025-04-15.
00:10:38 Aisha (Redwood AE): Great. Last bit — can we do an on-site feasibility call to walk the ops team through the installer and runbook?
00:10:46 Jorge (Capstone): Yes, ops would prefer an on-site for the initial rollout.
00:10:51 Aisha (Redwood AE): Perfect. Thanks everybody. Quick recap and we'll follow up with the artifacts and dates.

Action recap (spoken in call):
00:11:05 Aisha (Redwood AE): Next steps — we'll send the security pack and offline installer docs, Liam will run compatibility against your inventory, and we'll schedule the on-site feasibility run.

End of transcript.
